comments.text:
i know australia is likely better than other places, but im gonna give my two cents on why i think we're not just "green".

1. the housing crisis. i know this was mentioned, but it is HORRID. im single and on $100k a year, and even with all the FHB grants, i cant borrow more than $450k. id need a $150k deposit just for a standard house nearly 60km (37mi) out of the city. if im looking closer to the city, thats nearly a $500k deposit for a 1980 2 bedroom house. its insanity.

2. violence. while DEFINITELY lower than other countries, its on the rise. and rising fast. youth violence, machete attacks, political violence, all have been escalating like crazy. in the last 2 weeks, an MP was rammed into with a car, leaving her in the hospital for 5+ days in critical condition and losing both her legs. 2 MP offices have also been attacked, luckily no one else was hurt. machete attacks and murders continue despite efforts to stop them, and street/gang violence is still high.

3. national/state debt. theyre both at record highs, with national debt at over $1T and victorian state debt (where im from) expected to hit $200B alone by 2030. we are far outspending what we can afford.

4. immigration. i need to clarify before i get hate from others, i am pro-immigration! i just think we are letting in a LOT of people, and slowing down to let the housing market breathe isnt a horrible idea. australia was built on immigration and wouldn't survive without it, but we let in 500k people between 2022 and 2023. thats a LOT.

5. inflation, petrol & the cost of living crisis. petrol shot up after the iranian war (diesel at peaks of $3.30 AUD/litre or $8.80 USD/gallon, and petrol at peaks of $2.50 AUD/litre or $6.60 USD/gallon). inflation has been rising faster than wages, and there aren't a lot of protections for rental tenants or consumers. 

6. political, ethnic, and cultural division. the ramp up of division has been crazy recently. the rise of the far-right (one nation), the rise of islamophobia and antisemitism, the near collapse of the two-party system, its... honestly shocking, considering how we used to be such a peaceful and diverse place.

i know its definitely worse elsewhere and i am very grateful to live in australia, but i think its definitely worse than he made it out to be.
